attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, answering his own question.

semantics.note: 'In his view' keeps the 'I don't think so' opinion framing. He names no population, tools, task or speed measure, and the proposition adds none.

contract.note: The contract rightly declines to invent a population, task type, period or speed metric for a stated opinion. Calling it not scorable is fair to him.

evidence.note: This is the METR study he cites, and he describes it accurately. It covers one setting (experienced OSS developers, early 2025), so it cannot test his broad, unscoped opinion.

reviews.rationale: The statement is an opinion ('I don't think so') with no scope, population, tools or measure of speed. Scoring it would mean supplying a test he never gave. The METR study shows his citation is accurate but does not settle the general claim. Not adjudicable.

attribution.note: Zitron's own first-person words ('I believe') in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition drops 'I believe'. It also narrows 'lies of inference', a pun, to claims about capabilities, when the context points to popularity figures used to imply usefulness. This is an evaluative, rhetorical charge, not a checkable observation.

contract.note: The contract rightly finds no fair test: the phrase is undefined, and the marketing source, period and standard are all unstated. Declining to score is fair.

reviews.rationale: This is a stated belief built on a rhetorical pun ('lies of inference'). It names no scope, no period and no standard for what counts as a lie. Whether marketing was deceptive is a judgment about framing and intent that no agreed measure settles. Not adjudicable.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Maybe' hedges the $40B revenue figure only. 'No profit' is stated firmly and is scorable. The present-tense observation is correctly classed as observation.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: 'these companies' means generative AI model companies (chiefly OpenAI and Anthropic), and no profit is judged on 2025 net and operating results. Leaving the hedged revenue figure unscored is fair.

evidence.note: Press report of OpenAI's H1 2025 net loss of $13.5B, from shareholder disclosures as reported by The Information. It covers part of 2025 but squarely contradicts any profit.
FT, via The Register: OpenAI's H1 2025 operating loss of about $8B. Losses hold even without equity remeasurement.
Anthropic's 2025 net loss of $42B, from a leaked prospectus reported by Reuters. This is a company disclosure, not audited. Published 2026-09-28, before the evaluation date.
Anthropic's 2025 operating loss of $8.1B, excluding financing write-downs. Same source as e3.

reviews.rationale: Both leading generative AI model companies reported large 2025 losses: OpenAI (H1 net and operating losses) and Anthropic (full-year net and operating losses). The packet shows no profitable model company, so the firm 'no profit' part holds. The hedged $40B revenue figure is not scored. Smaller firms were not checked, but nothing contradicts the claim.
